def: The household (family) of the Prophet Muhammad. Seen by Shi'a Muslims as the rightful leaders of the Muslim community.
The Muslim name for God.
Collections of sayings by the Prophet Muhammad. Muslims see Muhammad as a role model, so look for guidance in his sayings.
A religious leader of the Muslim community (this is the Sunni Muslim word)
The holiest book in Islam
… are those who believe that the leadership of the Muslim community should be by the family of the Prophet Muhammad (Ahl al-bayt).
… believe Abu Bakr was the first of the four 'rightly guided' leaders of the Muslim community after Muhammad died.
God's justice. A Shi'a Muslim word. Muslims believe that God will make everything fair for everyone in the end.
Shi'a name for belief in the 124,000 prophets (messengers from Allah)
Belief that there is only one Allah and he is one being.
Shi'a belief that Allah selected people in the Prophet's family to be the rulers of the Muslim community. These rightful leaders are known as Imams in Shi'a Islam.
The Arabic for 'Five Roots'. These are the five most important beliefs for Shi'a Muslims.
Being kind. Muslims believe this of Allah - that he is kind to all people.
The belief that Allah acts in the world.
Being all-powerful. Muslims believe this of Allah - so he can do anything.
An action against Allah's will.
The name for a chapter in Arabic. The Qur'an has 114 ….
The belief that Allah is above and outside of his creation.
A messenger chosen by Allah to teach people about how to live the right life.
The Sunni Muslim name (equivalent of Nubuwwah in Shi'a) for the belief in the 124,000 prophets (messengers from Allah).
The Muslim name for the original Gospel of Isa (Jesus). Muslims believe this original is lost.
The name for all the books that Muslims see as holy - 'books of Allah'.
The scrolls of Ibrahim (Abraham) and Musa (Moses). Muslims believe they are lost.
The Muslim name for the Torah - 'scriptuires of Musa (Moses)'. Muslims believe these were revealed by Allah just for the Jewish people.
The … are the Psalms (which are in both the Jewish and Christian holy books). Muslims believe God sent these to Dawud (David).
The first prophet (messenger from Allah) in Islam. Also the first man.
(Abraham). An important prophet in Islam who is seen as a good example and who rebuilt the Ka'bah in Mecca.
(Ishmael). Ibrahim's son, who was willing to be sacrificed to Allah. Helped his father to rebuilt the Ka'bah in Mecca.
(Moses). An important prophet in Islam and seen as the main founder of Judaism. He received the Tarat (Torah - Holy Book for Jews).
(David). An important prophet who became king of the Jews and who was sent the Zabur (Psalms) holy book.
(Jesus). One of the most important prophets for Muslims. … did miracles and was sent the Injil holy book (Gospels).
The final and most important prophet for Muslims. Allah sent the Qur'an to him - Allah's final and complete message for all people on how to live.
The Arabic name for angels. Angels do tasks for Allah in the universe. Every person has angels on their left and right shoulder that record their good and bad actions.
(Gabriel). The archangel that Allah sends with messages for his prophets, including the Qur'an to Muhammad.
(Azrael). The archangel of death in Islam. Muslims believe that … takes people souls back to Allah at death.
(Michael). The archangel that Allah has given responsibility to keeps the order of natural processes going to support life.
The laws and plans of Allah for the universe. This includes natural laws that science studies, but also the destiny for things that Allah has already decided.
The Muslim word for life after death. This starts with the Day of Judgement, when, at the end of the world, Allah will bring all the dead back to life ot be judged.
Muslims believe that Allah will raise people to life after death.
The Arabic word for paradise. Muslims aim that when they die they will go to … (paradise) for ever.
The Arabic word for hell. This is a place of pain and suffering where Muslims believe people will go if they have not followed Allah's commands.
When people live together as a couple without being married.
The Arabic word for marriage. In Islam it is seen as a contract (legal agreement) between two people.
Having children.
When someone who has sex with someone other than the person they are married to.
Sexual relations between two people of the same sex
Sex before marriage
When two people who already have children marry, bringing their children together into a new family.
Where there is a mother, father, and their biological children, living together as one unit.
When a woman has another couple's fertilised egg placed into her womb so that she has the pregnancy for them (as they would not be able to have children otherwise)
The community of all Muslims around the world.
The Arabic word for the call to prayer
A ceremony for the birth of a baby.
Male circumcision - where the male baby's foreskin in surgically removed.
Islamic laws based on Muslim thinkers understanding of the Qur'an, Hadith (Muhammad's sayings) and Sunnah (acts of Muhammad in his life).
An old type of contraception where the penis is removed from the vagina before ejaculation.
Something that aims to stop sex resulting in pregnancy.
Thinking about what contraception to use and when to have children.
An approach to deciding on right and wrong that says people should always aim to try and do the most loving thing in each situation.
When it is declared that a marriage was never valid (true) in the first place.
Legally ending a marriage
Marrying again after being divorced from a previous marriage.
Believing that one gender (male or female) is less or more important than another
Treating people better or worse just because of their gender (whether they are male or female).
Encouraging others to do good actions. One of the ten obligatory acts for Shi'a Muslims.
Discouraging evil actions. One of the ten obligatory acts for Shi'a Muslims.
The most important rules of life for Shi'a Muslims.
Trying to associate only with good people. One of the ten obligatory acts for Shi'a Muslims.
Trying not to associate with bad people. One of the ten obligatory acts for Shi'a Muslims.
The five most important things that all Muslims try to do in their lives.
Statement of Muslim belief. One of the five pillars for Muslims.
The worst sin in Islam - treating something as equal to Allah or worshipping something other than Allah.
Prayer at five set times in the day. One of the five pillars for Muslims.
In Sunni Islam, this is the person who leads Salah (daily set prayers).
A special get-together and prayer held every Friday in mosques.
This is the name for facing towards Makkah during Salah (set prayers).
A set of movements and words in each Salah (set prayer).
Physical (and spiritual) washing before prayer in a specific ritual way.
A period of retreat in the mosque during the last ten days of Ramadan.
The Night of Power - remembering when the malaikah Jibril (angel Gabriel) first began to reveal the Qur'an to Muhammad.
The month of fasting. One of the five pillars of Islam.
Fasting - not eating or drinking. For Muslims during Ramadan, this means not eating or drinking during daylight.
A system for Shi'a Muslims where they pay an additional 20% of their savings to community causes.
Muslims who have less than a minimum amount (the …) are not expected to pay Zakah.
Extra voluntary charity donations that Muslims might make over and above Zakah (or Khums, for Shi'a Muslims).
Muslims are expected to donate 2.5% of their wealth to charitable causes. It is one of the Five Pillars of Islam. It literally means 'purification of wealth'.
The pilgrimage made by Muslims to Makkah during particular dates of the Muslim calendar. Doing … once is one of the Five Pillars of Islam, for Muslims who are physically and financially able.
A cube-shaped building in Makkah which Muslims believe was the first place of worship to Allah on Earth, and re-built by Ibrahim and Isma'il.
A journey to a place which is special for religious reasons.
Going around the Ka'bah in an anti-clockwise direction. Completed seven times during Hajj.
Trying hard to be the best person you can be - against temptations, for example.
The Arabic word for struggling, striving or trying hard.
Trying hard to stop evil in the world.
Shi'a Muslim date that remembers Imam Hussain's martyrdom (the death of Hussain, who they believe was one of Allah's chosen leaders for the Muslim community)
A festival at the end of Hajj that celebrates the faith of Ibrahim (Abraham) and Isma'il (Ishmael) to Allah. They were willing to sacrifice the most important things for Allah.
A festival celebrated at the end of Ramadan.
Shi'a Muslim festival remembering when the Prophet Muhammad chose Ali as the leader of Muslims.
Something that is useful or valuable for people to use. For example, oil, metal or wood.
Muslims who believe that the universe was made exactly as the Qur'an says and do not believe scientific accounts.

The most widely held scientific theory about the beginning of the universe. It says around 13.7 billion years ago everything was concentrated in a single, extremely small and hot point. This then began to expand and cool - and this has continued to this day.
The belief that life is special for religious reasons - for Muslims, because Allah has created it.
The scientific explanation for how all species of animal and plants have developed over billions of years from simple forms.
The idea that members of a species that are best suited to their environment will survive (and those who aren't well-suited, won't survive).
Ending a pregnancy by deliberately removing a foetus using surgery or drugs.
The first stage of human pregnancy - when the sperm fertilises the egg.
The Muslim belief that there is a point where the soul enters the foetus (developing human).
People who believe that a woman should be able to choose whether she has an abortion or not.
People who believe that the unborn child has a right to life.
Unexplained things thought to have spiritual or supernatural causes.
Mercy killing. When someone kills someone else, aiming to help them by doing so. Usually when someone has a terminal illness and has asked to be killed.
Care that aims to give as much comfort and help to people who have an incurable illness and are dying.
The Muslim belief that they should care for Allah's Earth as khalifahs (caretakers), so the next generation can enjoy it.
A way of deciding right and wrong. Utilitarians say people should choose to do things that will bring about the most happiness for the most people.
The Christian belief that God is one single God in three persons (Father, Son/Jesus and Holy Spirit).
The Son of God the Father - part of the Trinity. Christians believe Jesus came into the world as a human.
The Spirit of God - part of the Trinity. Christians believe this is the part of the Trinity that gives God's special gifts to people, such as healing and speaking God's words.
Some Christians believe that the world was created just as the Bible says - in six days in the order the Bible says. These are known as creationists.
The Christian belief that God (Jesus) became a human being on earth. This word is Latin for 'to become flesh (a physical body)'.
To be killed by being nailed to a cross and left to die. The Bible says that Jesus died this way.
Going against what God wants or has commanded. Christians believe … get in the way of people having a good relationship with God.
When Jesus went up to Heaven (40 days after his resurrection). The word literally means 'go up'.
When Jesus rose up from the dead - came back to life in his body. Christians believe all people will be resurrected after death.
Mending a broken relationship - making people 'at one' again. Christians believe that Jesus' death allows for people to be in a good relationship with God again.
The love of God, that God offers whether people deserve it or not.
When people are sorry for bad things they have done and do their best not to do them again.
Being saved. Christians believe that Jesus' death offers the chance of … from sin - to save people from a bad relationship with God and so Hell.
The day on which God judges people based on their choices in life - whether they chose to follow God or not.
A perfect place that lasts forever which Christians believe they will go when they die.
A place of punishment and pain away from God which lasts forever. Many Christians believe those who do not follow God will go there when they die.
A place which Roman Catholic Christians believe in. It is where the souls of the dead are punished to clean them of sins ready for Heaven.
Some Christians believe that everyone ('universally') will go to Heaven. This is because they think God's love and mercy means He would not send anyone to Hell forever.
Immortal means 'never die' or 'go on forever'. Many Christians believe people have souls that will live forever and go on to the afterlife after death.
All-good. Christians think God is all-good, so would never do anything bad.
These are bad things involving suffering that are done by people. For example, war.
These are bad things involving suffering that happen naturally (and are not done by people). For example, earthquakes.
All-powerful. Christians think God is all-powerful - God can do anything at all.
Making sure everyone gets what they deserve/what is fair - criminals and victims.
The rules that the government sets for the community. Protected by the police, the … Courts and punishments such as prison.
Mending broken relationships, replacing conflict with peace and anger with friendship.
Someone who is not sure whether God exists or not.
Someone who believes that God does not exist.
A type of atheist who looks to logic, science and the kind feelings in people to work out how to live.
Someone who is married having sex with someone other than who they are married to. Also called 'cheating' or having an affair.
To try to help someone back to a life following laws and being a good member of the community.
The human ability to have a choice in what we do. We are free to choose.
Putting people off from doing a crime by putting in place punishments for people who are caught. One of the aims of punishment.
Keeping people safe from the harm of crime by stopping the criminals by putting them in prison, for example. One of the aims of punishment.
Trying to change someone so that they change from a criminal life to one following the laws and being a good member of the community. One of the aims of punishment.
Doing wrong to someone who has done wrong (e.g. 'an eye for an eye'). One of the aims of punishment.
This type of response tries to help criminals stop doing crime, and to help victims, by having criminals meet their victims and hear about the victim's experiences and feelings.
The basic rights and freedoms that everyone in the world should have.
An approach to making choices about right and wrong that says people should always try to do the most loving thing in the situation.
Where someone who is accused of doing a crime is given a trial that is open to the public and where fair procedures to decide if they are guilty are used.
This is a trial where other ordinary citizens listen to the trial and decide whether the accused person is guilty of doing the crime or not (and so whether they will be punished).
Another name for the death penalty - where a government orders a person killed because of a crime they have done.
A statement of important Christian beliefs. The examples include the Nicene …, which Christians around the world say during worship.

A … is a grouping of Christians. Each Christian … will have slightly different beliefs and ways of worshipping. E.g. the Roman Catholic Church and the Church of England are the largest Christian … in the UK.
A form of Christian worship that follows a script of actions and words - often provided to worshippers in a booklet.
A form of Christian worship that has no set actions and words - no script.
A talk or teaching from a church leader, often looking at teachings in the Bible and applying them to issues Christians might face today.
When believers show their love, respect and faith to God. This is often in services held in churches.
A book written in 1562 that set out the important beliefs of the Church of England. These were slightly different than the beliefs of the Roman Catholic Church that the Church of England split from.
Apply holy oil to someone's head. It is seen as a sign of God's blessing the person and ceremony.
An important Christian ceremony, such as baptism. Roman Catholic Christians believe that God changes the spiritual world during a ….
The Christian ceremony that welcomes people in to the Christian community. Jesus was baptised in the Bible, so Christians are following this tradition.
Also called 'Mass' and 'Holy Communion'. This is the ceremony that remembers the Last Supper where Jesus shared bread and wine and said they were his body and blood.
Communicating with God
A journey done for a special religious reason - often to visit an important religious place.
This a part of the Christian year where Christians prepare for the festival of Christmas.
The Christian celebration of the visit of the wise men to the baby Jesus. The word literally means 'suddenly showing something amazing'.
This is the week before Easter. It remembers Jesus' time in Jerusalem the week before his death.
Someone doing the Christian 'mission' - looking to spread Christianity; often by trying to help those in need.
Speaking about the gospel : the life and story of Jesus from the Bible. As well as doing practical work to help those in need, missionaries evangelise.
Where Christians try to work together with other denominations. Some Christians hope that someday all the denominations can return to being one single Christian denomination.
A community of local Christians from one denomination, within a set area.
The local community of Christians, often centred on a holy building for meeting and worship.
Treating groups or individuals badly because of their religion, ethnicity or beliefs.
Mending broken relationships. Aiming to bring peace where there is conflict and friendship where there is anger. Ecumenism is the aim to mend the relationship between different denominations.
Someone who will not fight in a country's wars because their conscious tells them it is not morally right to fight.
Where a person stops feeling angry towards someone who has done wrong to them.
Someone who believes that violence, including war, is never right.
Someone who works to end conflict and violence to bring about peace. Jesus is called a … in the Bible.
A situation where two people or groups do not agree with each other over something they see as very important. This may involve violence.
Standing up against something that is seen as wrong without using any violence. It might mean doing marches, signing petitions, or even breaking laws that are seen as wrong (e.g. racist laws).

A Christian theory about when it would be just (to have justice/to be good/right) to fight a war and how that war would have to be fought. For example, it would have to be done for a good reason and would need to keep destruction to what was needed (and no more).
A war ordered by a religious leader to defend a religion or religious place; or to spread religious belief.
Weapons that can cause damage and death over a large area. For example, nuclear or chemical weapons.
An approach to choosing what is right or wrong that says people should try to the action that bring about the greatest amount of happiness, considering all the people affected.
Using violence, including against innocent civilians, for political or religious reasons.
